artworks.title: Chiron and Machaon among the physicians (Vienna Dioscurides)
artworks.description: Vienna Dioscurides (Austrian National Library, Cod. med. gr. 1, f. 2v), made in Constantinople for Anicia Juliana: the centaur Chiron, named in Greek, heads a circle of famous physicians, among them Machaon, the healer of the Greeks at Troy.

popCulture.title: Iliad (Machaon tends Menelaus)
popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Homer’s healer — son of Asclepius — draws the arrow from Menelaus and later falls wounded himself, so that Nestor must carry him from the fight. The Iliad remains Machaon’s primary cultural dossier; later medicine claimed him as a patron of surgery.
